# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-UPD-01 (EyePACS, faulty software update, United States)
- Period: week 13 (starting 2026-03-30)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift estimates that the AI's catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) at this clinic fell to 68% (band 53% to 82%), against a baseline of 90%. This estimate is predicted from 50 scans from this week alone. Expert grades for these scans have not yet arrived.

## 4. Potential patient impact
If the estimate is correct, approximately 2.87818 referable cases may have been missed. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
The clinic experienced a software update issue that altered downstream referral thresholds and behaviour, although image quality metrics like brightness (0.361 vs 0.373) and sharpness (0.000457 vs 0.000399) remained relatively stable. (Category: model degradation; confidence 80%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Referral rate dropped significantly from 0.685 to 0.36, representing a relative change of -0.474.
- Referral score mean decreased slightly from 0.193 to 0.188.
- Image quality and sharpness did not drop sharply, with quality actually showing a slight increase from 0.5 to 0.529.
- The evidence is weak regarding a pure population shift, as software updates are explicitly noted as a factor and visual inspection shows possible processing anomalies.

## 6. Action
Expected harm: 104348. Cost of review: 25000.
As the expected harm exceeds the cost of review, we recommend pausing the AI at this clinic and sending its scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Verify the integrity and version of the recently deployed software update at the clinic.
- [ ] Audit the decision threshold settings within the AI inference pipeline.
- [ ] Review a random sample of recent scans manually to confirm actual disease prevalence versus model output.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
- 7.4 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of transparency or interpretability
